data.body:
Reproduction attempt, 2026-10-26, same host and tree as the original failure (`b6e723ceb59` + unrelated eval-config diff):

```
pytest tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 4   (x3)
2 passed in 50.61s
2 passed in 47.99s
2 passed in 47.64s
```

Plus the earlier serial run immediately after the failure: `2 passed in 132.65s`.

So 4 attempts, 0 reproductions. That does NOT rule out any of the three candidate mechanisms — the original failure occurred inside a 57-minute full-suite run at 4-way concurrency with ~19.8k tests in flight, and a 2-test file at `-n 4` reproduces neither the host load nor the object-DB history of that run. It only establishes that the file is not deterministically broken on this tree.

The next experiment remains the one in the description: reproduce inside a full `make verify` with the Trace2 file preserved on failure, since the failing run's trace was lost with its `tmp_path`. Until that trace exists this stays unexplained rather than diagnosed.

Not blocking story `d279-4cf9-d1a6-4f7b`: that change touches eval config resolution (`llm/config_readers.py`, `llm/evals/**`, `_optional.py`, `_optionality.yml`, `rebar.toml`) and nothing in the store/git commit path this test exercises. Its Gerrit `Verified` vote runs the suite on Linux CI and is the authoritative gate.
